sections.title: A Meeting at UCLA
sections.content:
Steve Crocker expected the details of the network protocol outlined in NWG/RFC 33 to be ready within two weeks. Because people wanted a live presentation, he announced a network meeting at UCLA on Tuesday, March 17, at 9:00 a.m.

The meeting would present the protocol in enough detail to implement it unless participants found major flaws. Documentation would be available at the meeting.
sections.plainLanguage: The protocol authors planned an in-person presentation so network participants could hear the details and discuss problems.

sections.title: Attendance and Follow-Up
sections.content:
To make discussion easier, attendees were asked to limit participation to one programmer from each site. Participants were also advised to keep March 18 open in case discussion continued.

If the meeting did not make the documentation obsolete, it would be sent out as an NWG/RFC on March 20. The memo includes a telephone contact for help with arrangements.
sections.plainLanguage: Each site was asked to send one programmer. If the meeting did not require changes, the document would be circulated shortly afterward.

sections.title: A Coordination Memo
sections.content:
The text is limited to meeting arrangements and the planned presentation of a protocol. It does not contain the protocol details or prescribe network behavior.

Its publication as an RFC provides a dated record of how participants planned to discuss the proposal and decide whether its documentation needed revision.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo documents how the meeting was organized. The network rules themselves were expected in a separate document.
